title: Initialize the base part of a derived object
prompt: Device stores a positive id; Meter derives from Device and adds a nonnegative reading. The Meter constructor must pass its id to Device. Inputs satisfy those domains.
signature: class Device(int id); class Meter : public Device(int id,int reading)
starter:
#include <iostream>

class Device{int id_;public:explicit Device(int id):id_(id){}int id()const{return id_;}};class Meter:public Device{int reading_;public:Meter(int id,int reading):Device(1),reading_(reading){}int reading()const{return reading_;}};
solution:
#include <iostream>

class Device{int id_;public:explicit Device(int id):id_(id){}int id()const{return id_;}};class Meter:public Device{int reading_;public:Meter(int id,int reading):Device(id),reading_(reading){}int reading()const{return reading_;}};

tests.label: Id goes to base
tests.hint: Initialize Device from the received id.

tests.label: Second id
tests.hint: Do not hard-code one base id.

tests.label: Independent instances
tests.hint: Each object has its own base and derived data.

hints: A derived object contains a base subobject.
The colon after the constructor names the base constructor to call.
explanation: Device is built before the Meter fields. The base constructor receives the original id through the initializer list; no temporary or duplicate id is needed.
